vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: notion-sync
Version: 2.5.3

The notion-sync skill bundle is a well-structured set of tools for interacting with the Notion API using only built-in Node.js modules. It implements several security best practices, including a 'Path Safety Mode' in `notion-utils.js` to prevent path traversal and secure credential handling that avoids exposing tokens in process listings. The code logic is transparent, lacks external dependencies, and strictly aligns with the stated purpose of managing Notion workspaces.

llm.summary: The skill is mostly transparent Notion tooling, but it needs Review because one batch update command can modify many Notion records more broadly than the docs imply.

dimensions.detail: Searching, syncing, archiving, and updating Notion pages/databases fit the stated purpose, but batch-update.js can update up to 100 database pages and does not enforce a filter or dry run before writes.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The documentation presents --filter as required for query-mode batch updates, while the code treats it as optional, creating a real scope mismatch for high-impact Notion mutations.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install script, package installation, obfuscation, or hidden setup was found; the bundle is documentation plus Node.js scripts using built-in modules.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Node.js, Notion API access, and local markdown reads/writes are proportionate to the sync purpose; file access is workspace-limited by default with a documented manual unsafe-path override.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill uses a documented Notion token source, including auto-loading ~/.notion-token if present, and stores watch state in a documented local state file; no background daemon or hidden persistence was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Review before installing if your Notion workspace contains important shared or business data. Use a least-privilege Notion integration shared only with needed pages/databases, protect any token file, run batch updates with --dry-run first, always provide a narrow --filter, and avoid --allow-unsafe-paths unless you intentionally need files outside the current workspace.
llm.findings:
[RA2] expected: The long-lived ~/.notion-token behavior is real and auto-loaded if present, but it is plainly documented, chmod guidance is provided, and alternatives via stdin or environment variable are offered.
[TM1] expected: The --allow-unsafe-paths override is real, but it is an explicit flag, documented as intentional, and default file operations remain constrained to the current workspace.
[VirusTotal.clean] expected: VirusTotal telemetry reported no malicious or suspicious detections; this supports but does not determine the verdict.
[staticScan.clean] expected: The static scan reported no findings; local review still found the batch-update scoping concern from artifact code.
